notes.title: Development Update – August 2025
notes.content: [p][/p][previewyoutube="6ShZpbcYq5A;full"][/previewyoutube][h3]Hello everyone![/h3][p]We’d like to share some of the recent progress we’ve made on [b]Internal Incident[/b].[/p][p]The biggest milestone is a working [b]multiplayer system[/b]. We started implementing it fairly late in development, but after several weeks of work we managed to integrate it with our core gameplay.[/p][p]We also rebuilt the [b]monster spawning system[/b]. Instead of fixed spawners, creatures now appear dynamically in dark areas. Darkness itself is dangerous — monsters can emerge anywhere without light, and the system reacts to room lighting, the player’s presence, and flashlights. This creates a more natural and tense exploration experience.[/p][p]Finally, we’ve updated the [b]player hub[/b]. With more experience (and better assets) since the first version, we improved it to deliver a stronger atmosphere and smoother player experience.[/p][p]And one more thing — we’re actively working on a [b]publicly available playable demo[/b], so stay tuned![/p]

notes.title: Gameplay Early Demo
notes.content: [previewyoutube="_Ontm73N0Mc;full"][/previewyoutube][h3][b]We’re excited to share a first look at the gameplay of our game.[/b] [/h3][p]You can now watch the demo video on YouTube (and follow us there for future updates). This is an early version, but it already reflects the core direction we're aiming for. More features and improvements are on the way – and we’d love to hear your feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]The current version includes core systems such as shooting mechanics, AI-driven enemies, an inventory system, procedural level generation, dynamic objectives, and basic traders.[/p][p]We’re currently working on implementing multiplayer support.[/p][p]Looking ahead, we plan to add a quest system and narrative elements, as well as significantly improve the user interface.[/p]
